class_name: 範囲-範囲-ニワタッテ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: Presents a whole stretch of time as one unbroken span within which a state holds: 一年を通じて雨が多い. Its sibling にわたって instead measures out how far a single event extends, so a week of meetings is 一週間にわたって; 一週間を通じて would instead say a state held steady through the week. を通して is a near-equivalent, slightly more spoken and more willing to foreground an active means, while を通じて is the neutral/written choice and additionally has a separate 'via, through the good offices of' use with people and channels that does not belong to this span sense.

examples.ruby: この地域[ちいき]は一年[いちねん]を通[つう]じて湿気[しっけ]が多[おお]い。
examples.english: This area is humid all year round.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]は生涯[しょうがい]を通[つう]じて絵[え]を描[か]き続[つづ]けた。
examples.english: My grandfather went on painting his whole life long.

examples.ruby: 四季[しき]を通[つう]じて水温[すいおん]がほとんど変[か]わらない泉[いずみ]だ。
examples.english: It's a spring whose water stays at nearly the same temperature through all four seasons.

patterns.usage_note: Marks the extent an event covers, and the covered range can be time, territory, or a count of items, so it usually pairs with an explicit measure (三日間, 全域, 五十項目). Where を通じて says a state held uninterrupted through a period, にわたって stresses the sheer breadth of what happened. It comes from the verb 亘る/渡る, so the usual adnominal is にわたる (三日にわたる交渉); にわたっての also occurs but is the marked, less frequent option.

examples.ruby: 会議[かいぎ]は三日間[みっかかん]にわたって続[つづ]いた。
examples.english: The conference ran for three days straight.

examples.ruby: 停電[ていでん]の影響[えいきょう]は市内[しない]全域[ぜんいき]にわたった。
examples.english: The blackout's effects spread across the entire city.

examples.ruby: 調査[ちょうさ]は五十[ごじゅう]項目[こうもく]にわたって行[おこな]われた。
examples.english: The survey covered fifty separate items.
